﻿# 他把一个简单的聊天工具，变成了年入$5000万的客服平台

## 冷启动：刚毕业就看到了未来

2015年，Rashid 刚大学毕业。

在 Bangalore。

他注意到一个现象：

印度人不是用 WhatsApp。

是 live their digital lives through it。

这 spark 了一个 compelling question：

如果消费者大部分 digital time 都在 messaging apps。

Businesses 最终岂不是要在那里 meet them？

为了验证 messaging-based business communication 的 hypothesis。

他们 run an experiment。

后来证明 transformative。

Launch 了一个 consumer app 叫 Yellow Messenger。

让人们 discover and chat with local businesses using geolocation。

几个月内，500,000+ downloads。

50,000 monthly active users。

每天 thousands of chats。

最 remarkable 的部分？

所有这些对话，只有两个人手动处理。

这个 early traction 教会了他们 crucial lesson：

Consumers 已经 ready to interact with businesses through chat。

但 manually handling 这些 conversations wouldn't scale。

这 realization 让他们 develop 了 one of the first production-scale chatbots with NLP capabilities。

在2016年。

Well before WhatsApp officially opened its platform to businesses in 2019。

## 反直觉：有时候不做创新，反而能赢

Timing 和 location 完美配合。

Bangalore，India's Silicon Valley。

Low cost of living。

Rich tech ecosystem。

刚毕业反而是 advantage。

他可以 afford to be scrappy。

Living on minimal salary for years。

While building foundation of what would become Yellow.ai。

他们的旅程，从 simple consumer app 到 comprehensive AI platform。

Reflects a broader truth about entrepreneurship：

有时候最好的 business 不是 try to create something entirely new。

而是 carefully observe how people's behaviors are changing。

Build tools to support these evolving patterns。

虽然 WhatsApp 2019年才 open business platform。

他们已经 built robust chat automation system。

Across websites and mobile apps。

Positioning perfectly for messaging revolution。

What started as Yellow Messenger in 2016。

Has grown into company generating $40M-$50M ARR。

Helping businesses worldwide transform customer service through AI-powered voice and chat agents。

每天，他们的 AI agents handle countless conversations。

Across multiple languages and channels。

Learning and improving with each interaction。

Fascinating to see how small coding project evolved into solutions reshaping global customer service standards。

## 暴击：用别人的钱，养自己的梦

Financial aspect 是另一个 significant challenge。

但他们找到了 innovative solution：

Equity-free accelerators。

不是立即寻求 venture capital。

而是 strategically participated in three key programs：

**Startup Chile：**

$50,000 equity-free funding。

Valuable mentorship in Santiago。

Early support gave runway to experiment。

Without diluting ownership。

**Microsoft Accelerator：**

Instrumental in B2B pivot。

Offering office space in Bengaluru。

Plus $500,000 in Azure credits。

These credits essentially eliminated cloud infrastructure costs for first three years。

Allowing more investment in product development。

**SAP Accelerator：**

Crucial access to enterprise customers through their GTM team。

Helping understand enterprise needs。

Refine product accordingly。

Strategic use of accelerators allowed them to operate nearly four years without traditional office overhead。

Didn't establish own office until late 2019。

More importantly，provided powerful go-to-market motion。

Through integration with large organizations' sales stacks。

##  punchline：最狠的成功因素是人的决定

Building Yellow.ai 教会了 Rashid：

Single most critical factor in company's success lies in "people decisions"。

Specifically who you bring onboard。

How you develop them。

How you integrate new leadership。

最 significant challenge：

在不同 growth stages 做出正确的 hiring decisions。

Rapidly scaling 时，有些 setbacks 来自 hiring wrong leadership talent。

他们学到：

Bringing in senior leaders without proper context and integration。

Can be more damaging than having gaps in leadership team。

例如，曾经 hired senior executive。

First month 就 made sweeping changes to sales strategy。

Changes took nearly a year to course-correct。

Because they didn't align with core market understanding and customer needs。

**First major lesson：**

Developing internal talent 的巨大价值。

早期加入的团队成员，当公司还小的时候。

往往成为 most effective leaders。

They had deep contextual understanding of product、market、culture。

That external hires typically take 6-9 months to acquire。

**Second major lesson：**

Developing structured onboarding process for senior hires。

Now implement 90-day integration period。

New leaders focus on learning and understanding。

Before making major strategic decisions。

This approach significantly improved success rate with external hires。
